title: Alternating current
summary: Alternating current (AC) periodically reverses direction and varies in magnitude, forming the basis of most electric power delivery. Its voltage can be stepped up or down using transformers, enabling efficient long-distance transmission at high voltage and safe domestic use at 100–240 V. Standard waveforms are sinusoidal, though other shapes serve specialized applications. Three-phase generation uses offset coils to produce balanced currents, and distribution systems employ bonding and neutral conductors for safety. Frequencies typically range 50–60 Hz, with higher frequencies used in specialized contexts.

mechanisms.title: Voltage transformation for transmission efficiency
mechanisms.explanation: AC voltage can be increased or decreased with a transformer, allowing power to be transmitted at high voltage to reduce I²R losses in wires, then stepped down for safe consumer use.

mechanisms.title: Three-phase generation via offset coils
mechanisms.explanation: Three separate coils physically offset by 120° in a generator stator produce equal-magnitude currents 120° out of phase, enabling balanced power distribution and reduced neutral current under linear loads.
